name: OrderFirst — Distributed Microservices & Zero-Downtime CI/CD Platform
summary: A distributed restaurant ordering and table reservation system engineered with an event-driven microservices architecture, schema isolation, and automated zero-downtime deployment.
problem: Monolithic deployment coupled all services into slow all-or-nothing rebuilds, shared database schema bottlenecks, and downtime risks during releases.
solution: Decoupled into 6 independent microservices orchestrated by a Jenkins monorepo pipeline featuring selective git-diff change detection, parallel quality gates, and zero-downtime rolling updates.
devopsHighlights: Monorepo change detection: evaluates git diff to run parallel typecheck, unit tests, and Docker builds only for modified services
Zero-downtime rolling deployment using Docker Compose without restarting database, message broker, or untouched containers
Multi-platform container packaging (linux/amd64 & linux/arm64) and hardened dual-network isolation (zero exposed DB ports in prod)
applicationFeatures: High-concurrency table reservations protected by PostgreSQL btree_gist anti-overlap exclusion constraints
Fault-tolerant order processing with circuit-breaker resiliency and catalog inventory sync
Asynchronous transactional event processing and OTP dispatch via RabbitMQ messaging daemon
outcome: Eliminated monorepo release bottlenecks, reduced CI pipeline execution overhead, and enabled reliable, zero-downtime rolling production deployments.

name: DevTalk — Developer Community & CI/CD Platform
summary: A LinkedIn-inspired community where developers solve coding problems, publish blogs, and connect through jobs.
problem: Manual testing, scanning, image builds, and server commands made every release slow and inconsistent.
solution: A GitHub-triggered Jenkins pipeline tests, analyzes, scans, builds, and deploys the Docker Compose stack.
devopsHighlights: Push-to-deploy workflow using GitHub webhooks and Jenkins
Reusable stages for tests, SonarQube analysis, and Trivy scanning
Managed secrets and repeatable multi-container deployments
applicationFeatures: Accounts, posts, comments, and developer blogs
Real-time notifications for likes, comments, and applications
outcome: Turned manual releases into one repeatable, quality-gated path from commit to deployment.

name: Serverless URL Shortener — Hexagonal AWS Architecture & IaC Delivery
summary: A high-throughput, enterprise-grade serverless URL shortening and link management platform on AWS featuring pure functional hexagonal architecture, 100% Terraform IaC, and automated sub-second CI/CD.
problem: Monolithic URL shorteners carry idle compute costs, cold-start latency, database write collisions, and security risks from public S3 access and unpartitioned multi-tenancy.
solution: Architected a serverless hexagonal platform on AWS (Lambda, API Gateway v2, DynamoDB on-demand, CloudFront OAC, private S3) with 100% Terraform IaC and 208 automated unit/integration tests running sub-second.
devopsHighlights: 100% Terraform-managed cloud topology across Lambda, DynamoDB on-demand, private S3, and CloudFront with remote S3 state locking
Four automated GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows for PR plan summaries, state application, and atomic CloudFront cache invalidation
Zero public S3 access via CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC), scoped least-privilege IAM execution roles, and dynamic origin-locked CORS
applicationFeatures: Hexagonal architecture with curried pure functional use cases, zero OOP classes, and explicit Result<T, E> error handling monads
Collision-resistant 7-character short codes (62^7 ≈ 3.52 trillion unique URLs) with bounded retry and DynamoDB conditional writes
React 19 / Vite 8 single-page dashboard with accessible WAI-ARIA modals, optimistic UI updates, and stateless HS256 JWT auth
outcome: Achieved single-digit millisecond link redirection, near-$0 idle running costs, and 208 automated tests running in under 900ms without touching the network.
